name: Articles Supplementary to the Treaty of Chicago, 1833 (Treaty with the Chippewa, etc., September 27, 1833)
aka: Supplementary Articles of the 1833 Treaty of Chicago
promises: A further $100,000: $10,000 for individuals, $25,000 more for claims, $25,000 in goods, provisions and horses, and $40,000 in annuities of $2,000 a year for 20 years.

The Indians on the Michigan reservations were to remove within three years and, during that time, not be disturbed in their possession or in hunting on the lands, while the United States surveyed and sold them (supplementary Article 3).

breaches.what: The Indian Claims Commission valued the Michigan lands ceded under these articles (Royce Areas 188, 189 and 190, 104,960 acres) together with the main 1833 Chicago cession, found the total consideration of less than $3,000,000 for land worth $6,600,000 unconscionable and awarded $4,239,200.
breaches.whoFoundIt: Indian Claims Commission, Prairie Band of the Pottawatomie Tribe et al. v. United States, Dockets 15-C, 29-A and 71, 38 Ind. Cl. Comm. 128 (interlocutory order, 26 May 1976; final award, 23 June 1976)

source.title: Prairie Band of the Pottawatomie Tribe et al. v. United States, Dockets 15-C, 29-A, 71, Interlocutory Order (May 26, 1976)
source.publisher: Oklahoma State University Library, Indian Claims Commission Decisions

breaches.quote: so inadequate as to constitute unconscionable consideration

landTaken: 104,960 acres in southwestern Michigan (Royce Areas 188, 189 and 190), per the ICC interlocutory order of 26 May 1976.
compensation: Included in the $4,239,200 final award of 23 June 1976 for the whole 1833 Chicago cession (38 Ind. Cl. Comm. 389). See kappler-410.
today: See kappler-410 for the main treaty.

openQuestions: The Senate struck supplementary Article 4 when ratifying; what it provided was not checked.
The Pokagon Band's own history of how its people stayed in Michigan after these articles was not looked for; add it to nationVoice.
Audit 2026-11-08: the second promise left out that supplementary Article 3 also required the Indians to remove within three years and allowed survey and sale meanwhile; it now says so.
